transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

First switch it off and unplug it. Frozen produce at the back usually means cold air isn't circulating properly in the fridge section. The most common cause is a defrost fault where ice builds up on the evaporator coils (usually behind the freezer's rear panel), blocking the airflow that keeps the fridge cool but not freezing. Another possibility is simply that food is touching the cold back wall or blocking an internal vent. To tell these apart, please check inside the freezer compartment: is there a thick block of ice on the back wall, or does it look mostly clear with just light frost?
not sure tbh, cant really see the back wall in the freezer. food in there is solid as normal. do I really need to unplug it? its full of food

You don't need to unplug it just to look, but if there is a block of ice behind that back panel (which we can't see without emptying and defrosting), the fridge will keep freezing things until that ice melts. The fact that your lettuce and yoghurts are frozen solid strongly suggests cold air isn't circulating properly, which usually means the evaporator coils inside the freezer are iced over. The only way to confirm this is a full manual defrost: switch it off at the wall socket, move the food into cool bags with ice packs (or ask neighbours/family for help keeping it cold), put towels down inside and around the base, and leave both doors open until all ice has melted completely. Can you arrange to do this safely?
not really, its rammed after a big shop and i dont have cool bags. is there anything easier to try first?

If you can't do a full defrost yet, let's rule out the simple stuff first. Please check inside the fridge section: are any items touching the back wall or blocking the small vents usually found there? Also, is the fridge packed so tightly that air can't circulate between shelves? If food is touching the cold back wall or blocking those vents, moving them just an inch away often fixes the freezing immediately. If they are already clear and not overpacked, it's likely a defrost fault (ice building up behind the freezer panel), which will need a full defrost later to fix properly.
yes its rammed, stuff pressed right up against the vent at the back. the food that froze is up against the back wall near the vent slots

[Heading: Blocked air vents due to overpacking]
That confirms it. The cold air from the freezer is being blocked by your food, so it can't circulate into the fridge section properly and instead pools right at the back wall where you're standing. Please move everything away from that rear vent area immediately—just an inch or two of space is enough for the air to flow. Also, try not to pack items so tightly against each other on the shelves; cold air needs room to move around your food to keep it at a consistent temperature without freezing it solid. Once you've cleared the vents and rearranged the contents, leave the fridge running as normal. The frozen lettuce and yoghurts should thaw out and return to a normal chill within a few hours.
ok will clear the vents. dial inside is turned right up to max tho, kids may have moved it. should i turn it down?

[Heading: Blocked vents and max temperature setting]
Yes, please turn the dial down immediately. On most Hotpoint fridges, 'max' or 5 is the coldest setting; turning it to around 3 (or the middle of the scale) will stop the compressor from running so hard and let the fridge warm up slightly. Keep an eye on the milk or lettuce tomorrow—if they are still freezing after 24 hours with the dial at mid-range and vents clear, then it might be a thermostat fault, but for now, adjusting the setting is the fix.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
ok turned it to the middle and cleared the vents. after 2 days its better but one yoghurt still froze at the very back. is that normal?

[Heading: Likely residual cold spot or minor airflow issue]
It is not quite normal for food to freeze solid after you have cleared the vents and set the dial correctly, but a single item freezing while everything else is fine often just means that spot was holding onto cold air from when it was overpacked. Since you've had two days of improvement, give it another 24 hours with the dial at mid-range and plenty of space around the back vent. If that one yoghurt thaws out completely and stays thawed, you're good to go—just keep food away from the rear wall in future. However, if it freezes solid again within a day or two despite being clear of the vents, it suggests ice is building up behind the freezer's internal panel (a defrost fault), which will eventually need a full manual defrost to fix.
